network.name: Simplified downtown State College
network.disclaimer: Simplified State College network · synthetic traffic
notes: Schematic, axis-aligned geometry in metres (x = east, y = south). The real downtown grid is rotated roughly 45 degrees; it is drawn north-up here.
College Ave is modeled one-way westbound and Beaver Ave one-way eastbound (see https://ecode360.com/32902839).
Intermediate streets (Burrowes, Fraser, Garner, ...) are intentionally omitted; block lengths are approximate.
Allen St and Pugh St end at College Ave (campus side is not a vehicle road in this model).
Signal timings, lane assignments and turn permissions are simulation assumptions, not municipal timing plans.

selectionRule: Candidate must be a valid policy.
Screen: mean training score must beat the champion's training score.
Development score must improve on the champion by at least 1%.
Must win (lower score) on at least 50% of paired development scenarios.
Mean completion fraction may not drop by more than 0.5 percentage points.
Side-street (Allen/Pugh origin) P95 wait may not exceed champion × 1.1 + 2 s.
Overall P95 wait may not exceed champion × 1.1 + 2 s.
If several candidates pass in one round, the lowest development score becomes champion.
scoreDefinition: Primary score = total stopped vehicle-seconds (speed < 0.5 m/s inside the network, plus all time spent in external entry queues) ÷ total scheduled vehicles. Lower is better. Every controller gets the same 900 s demand horizon and 300 s drain; unfinished vehicles keep accumulating stopped time and are reported as residual backlog.

championHistory.reason: Starting champion: stronger baseline on the development suite

candidates.name: coord-wave-90
candidates.hypothesis: Enabling a 90 s coordination plan that aligns phase-0 (arterial) green starts with platoon travel times (College WB: C_PUG 40 -> C_ALL 54 -> C_ATH 0; Beaver EB: B_ATH 0 -> B_ALL 36 -> B_PUG 50), and giving C_ATH and B_ATH the same offset so both Atherton directions progress simultaneously (10.4 s link < green), will reduce stops on the dominant College WB / Beaver EB flows without starving side streets.
candidates.explanation: Keeps the champion's adaptive parameters at all six intersections; only enables coordination.cycle=90 with six phase-0 'green-band' windows: C_PUG offset 40 len 30 bonus 10, C_ALL offset 54 len 30 bonus 10, C_ATH offset 0 len 45 bonus 12, B_ATH offset 0 len 45 bonus 12, B_ALL offset 36 len 30 bonus 10, B_PUG offset 50 len 30 bonus 10. Offsets equal free-flow platoon travel times (14.3 s and 35.7 s links), so a platoon leaving an upstream phase-0 green arrives as the downstream window opens; the longer/higher-bonus windows at the two spillback-critical Atherton intersections (C_ATH College WB 8.6k, B_ATH Beaver EB 9.7k stopped veh-sec) also let their phase-0 green extend toward maxGreen. Fixed blocks are retained (cycle 90) with offsets/splits consistent with the coordinated plan in case a mode change is ever tested.

candidates.name: coord-arterial-wave
candidates.hypothesis: The champion is fully uncoordinated, so Beaver EB at B_ATH (9694 stopped veh-s/ep) and College WB at C_ATH (8594) repeatedly stop platoons that were just released upstream. Adding a soft coordination layer (90 s cycle, phase-0 bonus windows placed on the measured link travel times, C_PUG->C_ALL->C_ATH and B_ATH->B_ALL->B_PUG) will let those platoons clear several signals without stopping, cutting arterial stopped time without taking green away from side streets (windows cover only ~40 s of 90 s and leave adaptive logic in charge outside the window).
candidates.explanation: Changed vs champion (all adaptive blocks, weights, holds and hysteresis left untouched to isolate the effect): (1) coordination.enabled true, cycle 90 s matching the fixed cycle; (2) six phase-0 bonus windows forming green waves on the two one-way arterials using the given link travel times: C_PUG@0 (len 45, bonus 20), C_ALL@14 (40, 18), C_ATH@50 (40, 20), B_ATH@45 (45, 20), B_ALL@81 (40, 18), B_PUG@5 (35, 15). Offsets: College WB chain 0 +14.3 +35.7; Beaver EB chain 45 +35.7 +14.3 (mod 90). C_ATH@50 and B_ATH@45 are near-aligned so the Atherton NB/SB phases at the two cross-street signals also line up. Expected effects: fewer stops/delay on College WB and Beaver EB platoons, less residual queue feeding the short storage links (col_pug_all 34 veh, bea_all_pug 34 veh), lower spillback at bea_in_w (113 s) and col_in_e (65 s); bonuses are moderate (~20 vs a 20-veh queue score) so side-street phases can still preempt when their queues dominate.

candidates.name: side-wait-protect-v1
candidates.hypothesis: Raising oldest-wait weight and adding a small side-phase bias at Allen/Pugh intersections will trigger earlier service to side streets, reducing their P95 and max waits; rebalancing max green toward higher-volume side approaches at B_ALL/B_PUG increases side discharge capacity, while arterials retain priority via queue and approaching terms.
candidates.explanation: C_ALL/C_PUG: oldestWait 0.04->0.15, phaseBias [0,0]->[0,1.5], hysteresis 6->5, maxGreen unchanged. B_ALL: maxGreen [50,35]->[42,44], oldestWait 0.15, phaseBias [0,1.5], hysteresis 5. B_PUG: maxGreen [50,35]->[40,44], oldestWait 0.15, phaseBias [0,1.5], hysteresis 5. C_ATH/B_ATH: oldestWait 0.04->0.08 to reduce tails. Coordination remains disabled.

candidates.name: coord-wave-90-v2
candidates.hypothesis: The current champion is uncoordinated, so College WB and Beaver EB platoons released upstream frequently reach the next signal on red, causing the dominant stopped time at C_ATH (8594 veh-s) and B_ATH (9694 veh-s). Re-enabling a 90 s coordination plan with windows offset by the measured link travel times (14.3 s / 35.7 s) plus ~3 s start-up loss, using a moderate bonus, should let these platoons clear all three signals without stopping, while leaving green shares unchanged so side-street and overall P95 waits are preserved.
candidates.explanation: Coordination enabled, shared cycle 90 s. Add phase-0 (arterial) bonus windows at all six signals: C_PUG offset 40, C_ALL offset 54, C_ATH offset 0 (College WB travel chain 40->54->0); B_ATH offset 0, B_ALL offset 36, B_PUG offset 50 (Beaver EB chain 0->36->50). Window length 45 s, bonus 15. All adaptive parameters, max greens [50,35], weights, minHold 16, hysteresis 6 and the fixed-block fields are kept exactly at the champion values, so side streets keep the same effective green and the 90 s max-red guarantee; expected effect is fewer stops on the two dominant one-way arterials and on Atherton (both Atherton phases stay simultaneously timed because C_ATH and B_ATH share offset 0).

candidates.name: queue-discharge-priority-v1
candidates.hypothesis: Green should follow actual discharge demand: weighting standing queues about 3x more than 120 m arrivals makes the controller hold green for the approach that can actually clear vehicles (2 s/veh/lane) instead of chasing arrivals that are still 15-35 s away, and a slightly stronger downstream-occupancy penalty keeps the short 34-veh receiving links (col_pug_all, bea_all_pug) from being fed into spillback. Both effects target the bursty scenarios where the champion scores worst (78.0, 46.2).
candidates.explanation: All six intersections (unchanged minHold 16, maxGreen [50,35], hysteresis 6, phaseBias [0,0], fixed blocks and disabled coordination kept identical to champion): weights.queue 1 -> 1.5 (prioritise vehicles that can discharge now), weights.approaching 0.8 -> 0.5 (stop rewarding far-away arrivals that will re-stop), weights.oldestWait 0.04 -> 0.05 (mild anti-starvation, no side-street bias added), weights.downstream 0.8 -> 0.9 (stronger suppression of phases whose receiving link is occupied, to cut spillback at C_PUG/B_ATH). Expected: fewer wasted green seconds on empty approaches, shorter arterial queues at C_ATH/B_ATH, less spillback on the 132 m links, with no new side-street bias so side P95 should not regress.

candidates.name: r2-arterial-hold-tune
candidates.hypothesis: The two Atherton intersections (C_ATH, B_ATH) are overloaded on both phases and suffer from frequent switching under bursty demand; raising min hold to 20 s, hysteresis to 8, and max greens to 55/40 will reduce clearance and start-up losses and clear queues more efficiently, while leaving Allen/Pugh side-street intersections untouched so their P95 waits are not degraded.
candidates.explanation: Changed only C_ATH and B_ATH adaptive parameters: minHold 16→20, maxGreen phase0 50→55, phase1 35→40, hysteresis 6→8. Other four intersections keep champion values. Expected effect: longer minimum greens and higher switching margin reduce the number of phase switches (each costing 5 s clearance and 2 s start-up) at the network's two busiest intersections, lowering stopped vehicle-seconds primarily in bursty and arterial scenarios. Side streets are unaffected because they are controlled by the unchanged Allen/Pugh intersections.

candidates.name: r3-atherton-hold-tune-2
candidates.hypothesis: Further reducing switching losses at the two Atherton intersections by increasing min hold, max greens, and hysteresis will cut the dominant stopped time on both phases (College WB/Beaver EB and Atherton), especially in bursty scenarios, without degrading side-street P95 because the cross-street phase also receives a longer maximum green.
candidates.explanation: At C_ATH and B_ATH: minHold 20->22, maxGreen [55,40]->[60,45], hysteresis 8->10. Other intersections and coordination unchanged. Expected: lower stopped vehicle-seconds at the main bottlenecks, improved bursty scores, stable or slightly improved side-street P95 due to more discharge capacity on both phases.

candidates.name: r3-arterial-discharge-hold
candidates.hypothesis: The two Atherton intersections are the network's discharge bottlenecks: their phase-0 legs (College WB at C_ATH, 8580 stopped veh-s; Beaver EB at B_ATH, 8733 stopped veh-s) carry the largest queues and their spillback blocks the whole upstream corridor (C_ALL 65 s and C_PUG 45 s blocked-by-downstream). Allowing a little more phase-0 green and still longer/steadier holds at these two intersections will discharge more vehicles per switch (fewer 5 s clearance + 2 s start-up losses) and unblock the upstream corridor, without touching Allen/Pugh logic that protects side-street waits.
candidates.explanation: Changed only the two Atherton intersections; all weights, Allen/Pugh settings and coordination left identical to the champion. C_ATH: minHold 20 -> 22, hysteresis 8 -> 10, maxGreen [55,40] -> [58,42], phaseBias [0,0] -> [0.5,0] (slight favour to College WB, whose downstream is a free exit so its green is never wasted). B_ATH: minHold 20 -> 22, hysteresis 8 -> 10, maxGreen [55,40] -> [58,44], phaseBias [0,0] -> [0.5,0] (slight favour to Beaver EB, the worst entry queue, 23 s mean wait / 90 s spillback). Expected effects: fewer phase switches on the two dual-saturated Atherton intersections (each switch costs 5 s clearance plus 2 s start-up), fuller discharge of the dominant queue at each, and reduced spillback into col_all_ath / col_pug_all / ath_b_c, so C_ALL and C_PUG keep discharging instead of being blocked. Atherton's competing phase stays protected by the unchanged oldest-wait term (0.04), min green 10 s and the 90 s forced-service rule; side-street P95 should be unaffected because Allen/Pugh parameters are untouched.

candidates.name: r3-side-wait-responsive
candidates.hypothesis: Side-street tail waits (Allen/Pugh P95 ~103-146 s in bursty scenarios) are caused by the low oldest-wait weight (0.04) letting arterial queues monopolize green until the simulator's 90 s forced switch; raising oldest-wait sensitivity and slightly shortening minHold/hysteresis at the four Allen/Pugh intersections, plus shifting a few seconds of max green to the side phase, will let side queues discharge one cycle earlier and cut P95/max waits without starving the arterials (their mean waits at these nodes are only 4-8 s).
candidates.explanation: At C_ALL, C_PUG, B_ALL, B_PUG only: oldestWait 0.04->0.12 (side waits now compete with arterial queues), hysteresis 6->4 (switch sooner when a side approach has aged), minHold 16->14 (faster burst response), maxGreen [50,35]->[46,38] (small green shift toward the single-lane side phase to drain accumulated queues). Atherton intersections (C_ATH, B_ATH) and coordination left exactly as champion. Expected: lower side-street P95/max and better bursty-scenario robustness; arterial stopped time roughly unchanged because these nodes have low arterial mean waits and spillback is not aggravated.

candidates.name: r4-atherton-pair-align
candidates.hypothesis: Atherton NB/SB through trips stop twice because the phase-1 (Atherton) greens at C_ATH and B_ATH drift freely across the 112 m / 10.4 s link; pinning both intersections' phase-1 green into one identical coordination window aligns them so a platoon released at one Atherton node arrives during the other's green, cutting a large share of the 13.7k veh-s (28% of total) Atherton stopped time without reallocating arterial green.
candidates.explanation: Keeps every adaptive parameter of the champion (minHold 20/hysteresis 8/maxGreen [55,40] at C_ATH & B_ATH; minHold 16/hysteresis 6/maxGreen [50,35] at C_ALL, C_PUG, B_ALL, B_PUG; unchanged weights) so College WB and Beaver EB green shares and side-street service are untouched. Adds coordination at the existing 90 s cycle with only two soft windows, both on the Atherton phase: C_ATH phase 1 and B_ATH phase 1, offset 10 s, length 40 s (equal to each node's phase-1 maxGreen), bonus 12 (larger than the 8 s hysteresis, so phase 1 is reliably concurrent in that interval while phase 0 keeps the remaining ~50 s for College WB / Beaver EB). Expected effect: simultaneous (aligned) Atherton greens at the two nodes, eliminating the second stop for NB and SB through platoons, reducing blocked-by-downstream time on ath_b_c/ath_c_b and the associated spillback, while cycle length stays 90 s and side-street phases lose no window.

candidates.name: r4-allen-pugh-hold-steady
candidates.hypothesis: The accepted r2-robustness fix (longer minHold, larger hysteresis, larger maxGreen) cut switching losses at the two Atherton nodes and won 4/4 dev scenarios; the four Allen/Pugh nodes still use the old twitchy settings (minHold 16, hysteresis 6, maxGreen 50/35) and are the remaining source of clearance + start-up losses and of the spillback/blocked-by-downstream seen at C_PUG (57 s spillback, 45 s blocked) and C_ALL (65 s blocked). Applying a milder version of the same recipe there should discharge queues in fewer, longer greens without taking green away from side streets (hysteresis is symmet
candidates.explanation: Changed only the four Allen/Pugh intersections (C_ALL, C_PUG, B_ALL, B_PUG), leaving C_ATH and B_ATH exactly as in the champion: minHold 16 -> 18 s, hysteresis 6 -> 9 (more margin needed to switch away from the current green, fewer 5 s clearance + 2 s start-up losses), maxGreen [50,35] -> [52,38] so a phase that is still discharging is not cut off prematurely. Weights (queue 1, approaching 0.8, oldestWait 0.04, downstream 0.8), phaseBias [0,0] and coordination (disabled) are unchanged. Expected effect: fewer switches and less re-queuing at the four remaining intersections, lower stopped veh-s especially in bursty scenarios, with side-street P95 bounded by the simulator's 90 s forced-service rule.

candidates.name: r4-allen-pugh-hold-steadier
candidates.hypothesis: The switching-loss reduction that worked at the two Atherton nodes (minHold 20 / hysteresis 8) has not been applied to the four Allen/Pugh nodes, which still run the twitchier setting (minHold 16 / hysteresis 6); there the arterials have only 4-8 s mean wait while side approaches wait 16-21 s, so a longer committed green (minimum 20 s once a phase starts, and a wider margin before leaving it) cuts the 7 s clearance+start-up cost per avoided switch and gives the one-lane side phases a longer contiguous discharge window, lowering both switch losses and side-street tail waits without needing any
candidates.explanation: Changed only the four Allen/Pugh intersections (C_ALL, C_PUG, B_ALL, B_PUG), keeping the champion's proven Atherton settings (C_ATH/B_ATH minHold 20, hysteresis 8, maxGreen 55/40) untouched. At each of these four nodes: adaptive.minHold 16 -> 20 s and adaptive.hysteresis 6 -> 8. maxGreen ([50,35]), weights (queue 1, approaching 0.8, oldestWait 0.04, downstream 0.8), phaseBias [0,0], modes, fixed blocks and coordination (disabled, 90 s, no windows) are all unchanged. Expected effects: (1) fewer switches per hour -> saved 5 s clearance + 2 s start-up loss each; (2) side phases (Allen NB, Pugh NB/SB, one lane each) get longer contiguous greens, so their bursty queues clear in fewer services, improving side-street P95/max; (3) extra hold on the arterial phase is cheap at these nodes because their arterial mean waits are only 4-8 s (C_ALL College WB 6.2, C_PUG College WB 8.3, B_ALL Beaver EB 7.0, B_PUG Beaver EB 4.1), so arterial P95 and completion should be preserved, and the simulator's 90 s forced switch still bounds any starvation.
